notes: Curated starter dataset. Distances, elevations and coordinates are approximate and should be verified (e.g. against USFS / OpenStreetMap) before production use. Difficulty is computed automatically from distance + elevation gain (see server/src/difficulty.js).

trails.name: Mount Timpanogos via Timpooneke
trails.description: The classic route to the summit of Timp, the second-highest peak in the Wasatch. Climbs past Scout Falls and through alpine basins full of wildflowers and mountain goats before a rocky final ridge to the summit hut.
trails.tips: Start before sunrise to beat afternoon thunderstorms. The final ridge is exposed and the saddle often holds snow into July.

trails.name: Mount Timpanogos via Aspen Grove
trails.description: Steeper and more dramatic than Timpooneke, this route passes a string of waterfalls and Emerald Lake below the Timp glacier before topping out on the summit.
trails.tips: Snowfields linger near Emerald Lake well into summer — microspikes are helpful early season.

trails.name: Emerald Lake via Aspen Grove
trails.description: A big day without the summit push: switchback past dozens of cascades to the turquoise lake tucked beneath Timp's eastern cliffs.
trails.tips: Great turnaround option if summit weather turns.

trails.name: Scout Falls
trails.description: A short, family-friendly section of the Timpooneke trail leading to a tall waterfall that is strongest in early summer.
trails.tips: Best flow in June after snowmelt.

trails.name: Stewart Falls
trails.description: One of the most popular hikes in the county: an easygoing walk through aspen groves to a two-tiered 200-foot waterfall below Timp's east face.
trails.tips: Spectacular in late September when the aspens turn gold. Parking fills early on weekends.

trails.name: Timpanogos Cave Trail
trails.fee: National Monument cave tour ticket required
trails.permit: Reserve cave tour tickets in advance; trail open seasonally (roughly May–Sept).
trails.description: A steep paved trail climbing the side of American Fork Canyon to the entrance of the Timpanogos Cave system, famous for its helictites.
trails.tips: Bring a jacket — the cave is about 45°F year-round.

trails.name: Bridal Veil Falls
trails.description: A short, flat stroll along the Provo River Parkway to the base of a double-cataract waterfall that drops over 600 feet.
trails.tips: In winter the falls freeze into an ice-climbing destination.

trails.name: Y Mountain Trail
trails.description: Twelve switchbacks up the mountainside to the giant block Y above BYU, with sweeping views of Provo and Utah Lake.
trails.tips: No shade — go early in summer, or for sunset.

trails.name: Kyhv Peak (formerly Squaw Peak)
trails.description: A steep climb out of Rock Canyon to the prominent peak overlooking Provo — one of the best views of Utah Valley.
trails.tips: The upper section is loose and steep; trekking poles help on the descent.

trails.name: Rock Canyon Trail
trails.description: A rugged canyon of towering quartzite walls right at the edge of Provo, popular with climbers and trail runners. Turn around anywhere for a shorter outing.
trails.tips: Shady in the morning; the stream runs strong in spring.

trails.name: Battle Creek Falls
trails.description: A quick canyon hike from Kiwanis Park to a pretty 50-foot waterfall. Continue upward toward Big Baldy for more of a workout.
trails.tips: Wet and muddy near the falls in spring.

trails.name: Grove Creek Trail
trails.description: Switchbacks climb high above a narrow canyon with views across Utah Valley, passing a seasonal waterfall along the way.
trails.tips: Exposed lower switchbacks get hot by mid-morning.

trails.name: Big Baldy
trails.description: Climb past Battle Creek Falls to the bald summit on Timp's southwest shoulder, with big views of the Timp massif and the valley below.
trails.tips: Route finding near the top can be tricky — download a map.

trails.name: Dry Canyon (Lindon)
trails.description: A steady climb through a rocky canyon with maples that light up red in autumn.
trails.tips: Little shade — best on cool days.

trails.name: Silver Lake (American Fork Canyon)
trails.description: From Silver Lake Flat Reservoir, climb through forest into the Lone Peak Wilderness to a clear alpine lake ringed by granite.
trails.tips: The road to Silver Lake Flat is rough but passable for most cars when dry.

trails.name: Silver Glance Lake
trails.description: Continue past Silver Lake up steep, faint trail and boulder fields to a tiny high cirque lake beneath the Pfeifferhorn ridge.
trails.tips: Steep scrambling — not for beginners.

trails.name: Box Elder Peak
trails.description: An 11,000-footer with far fewer crowds than Timp, offering a jaw-dropping view straight across to Timpanogos and down into the Lone Peak Wilderness.
trails.tips: The upper ridge is steep and loose.

trails.name: Lone Peak via Schoolhouse Springs
trails.description: One of the toughest day hikes in the Wasatch, ending with an exposed class 3 granite scramble to the summit of Lone Peak.
trails.tips: Carry plenty of water; there is little on the upper route.

trails.name: Horsetail Falls (Dry Creek)
trails.description: A steady climb up Dry Creek Canyon to a long, wispy waterfall spilling down granite slabs.
trails.tips: The falls are best in May and June.

trails.name: Lake Hardy
trails.description: Continue past Horsetail Falls up to a stark granite basin holding Lake Hardy, below Lone Peak's eastern cirque.
trails.tips: Upper trail fades in boulder fields — bring GPS.

trails.name: Tibble Fork Reservoir Loop
trails.description: An easy loop around a mountain reservoir popular for paddleboarding and picnics.
trails.tips: Great warm-up before the many trails starting nearby.

trails.name: Pine Hollow Trail
trails.description: A quiet loop through pine and aspen forest with views of Timp's north face — a local favorite for fall colors.
trails.tips: Shared with mountain bikers; stay alert on descents.

trails.name: Cascade Springs
trails.description: Boardwalks wind over crystal-clear limestone terraces where millions of gallons of spring water bubble up every day.
trails.tips: Look for trout in the pools. Partly wheelchair accessible.

trails.name: Big Springs Hollow
trails.description: A gentle loop through meadows and aspen with views of Timp's back side — also a popular snowshoe route in winter.
trails.tips: Wildflowers peak in early July.

trails.name: Lambert Park Loop
trails.description: A web of rolling singletrack through oak and wildflower meadows above Alpine — great for easy trail runs.
trails.tips: Spring wildflowers here are excellent.

trails.name: Fifth Water Hot Springs
trails.description: Follow Sixth Water and Fifth Water creeks to a series of milky-blue natural hot spring pools beside waterfalls.
trails.tips: Very busy on weekends. Pack out all trash. Winter access adds miles when the road is gated.

trails.name: Payson Lakes Loop
trails.description: A flat loop around a cluster of high mountain lakes on the scenic Nebo Loop, perfect for families.
trails.tips: Combine with a scenic drive along the Nebo Loop in fall.

trails.name: Grotto Falls
trails.description: A tiny trail with a big payoff: a waterfall pouring into a mossy rock grotto, reached after a few creek crossings.
trails.tips: Wear shoes that can get wet.

trails.name: Mount Nebo via North Peak Trail
trails.description: The highest peak in the Wasatch Range sits on the Utah–Juab county line. This route climbs open ridges with huge views in every direction.
trails.tips: Exposed ridge — watch for lightning.

trails.name: Provo Peak
trails.description: Short and brutally steep, this route from the Squaw Peak Road climbs an unrelenting ridge to the highest point directly above Provo.
trails.tips: High-clearance vehicle recommended for the access road.

trails.name: Buffalo Peak
trails.description: An easy summit off the Squaw Peak Road with excellent views of Timp, Cascade and Provo Peak.
trails.tips: One of the best sunset-to-effort ratios around.

trails.name: Slate Canyon
trails.description: A less-crowded alternative to Rock Canyon, climbing a narrow canyon on the southeast side of Provo.
trails.tips: Watch for mountain bikers on the lower trail.

trails.name: Santaquin Peak
trails.description: A long ridge walk from Payson Canyon to a summit overlooking the south end of Utah Valley and Mount Nebo.
trails.tips: Bring all your water.

trails.name: Mahogany Mountain
trails.description: A lesser-known summit on the north shoulder of Timp with excellent views into American Fork Canyon.
trails.tips: Great fall-color hike in late September.

trails.name: Bonneville Shoreline Trail (Provo)
trails.description: Rolling bench trail following the ancient shoreline of Lake Bonneville above Provo and Orem — a staple for trail runners.
trails.tips: Many access points; do any section as an out-and-back.

trails.name: Provo River Parkway
trails.description: A paved path from Utah Lake State Park up through Provo and into Provo Canyon, passing Bridal Veil Falls. Ideal for long runs.
trails.tips: The canyon section is the most scenic stretch.

trails.name: Murdock Canal Trail
trails.description: A smooth paved trail along the old Murdock canal with mile markers and constant views of Timp — a favorite for runners.
trails.tips: Mile markers make it great for tempo runs.

trails.name: Jordan River Parkway (Lehi)
trails.description: Flat paved trail following the Jordan River from Utah Lake north toward the Point of the Mountain, with good bird watching.
trails.tips: Connects north into Salt Lake County for very long runs.

trails.name: Spanish Fork River Trail
trails.description: A peaceful paved path along the Spanish Fork River through parks and farmland.
trails.tips: Good option for an easy recovery run.
